pairs.description: Goldenseal significantly reduces metformin blood concentrations by approximately 25 percent, potentially reducing glycemic control in diabetic patients.
pairs.mechanism: Inhibition of organic cation transporters (OCT1/OCT2) and hepatic uptake by goldenseal isoquinoline alkaloids like berberine.

pairs.description: Goldenseal inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein, significantly elevating blood levels and toxicity of cyclosporine.
pairs.mechanism: Potent intestinal and hepatic CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition by berberine and hydrastine constituents.

pairs.description: Clinical studies demonstrate goldenseal markedly inhibits CYP3A4, substantially increasing oral midazolam exposure and sedative duration.
pairs.mechanism: Inhibition of intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes, reducing first-pass metabolism of oral midazolam substrate.

pairs.description: Goldenseal alkaloids inhibit P-glycoprotein-mediated renal and biliary excretion of digoxin, elevating serum cardiac glycoside levels.
pairs.mechanism: P-glycoprotein efflux pump inhibition resulting in increased absorption and decreased renal clearance of digoxin.
